title: Preface
summary: The partial document covers a technical review for Riverdale Bicycle Works in 2025, including sections on company overview, manufacturing sites, model lineup for the year, quality and recall information, financial summary, and research and outlook.

title: Company Overview
summary:
The main points covered in the partial document are:
- Company name and founding: Riverdale Bicycle Works was founded in 1998 by Elena Marsh.
- Products and manufacturing: The company designs and assembles bicycle frames in aluminium and carbon fibre.
- Distribution: They sell through 240 independent dealers in the United Kingdom and Ireland.
- Employee details as of 2025: The company employed 214 people, with breakdowns in production (68), assembly and finishing (41), and other roles (105).
- Additional production site: Acquired a second production site in Porto, Portugal, in 2019 to serve continental customers.

title: Manufacturing Sites
summary: The partial document covers manufacturing sites, specifically the Leeds and Porto plants. Key points include the operations of the Leeds plant, which has two welding lines for different types of frames, and the production capacity and output for 2025. The Porto plant, acquired in 2019, focuses on carbon lay-up and paint, with its current production utilization. Both sites use a shared quality laboratory for fatigue tests.

title: Model Lineup 2025
summary: The partial document covers the 2025 model lineup for a cycling brand, including five models: Kestrel 700 for road use, Harrier ST for gravel, Owl 26 for children, Peregrine E for electric needs, and Swift 3 for city riding. Each model is described by its type, weight, price, and additional features like battery capacity for the electric model.

title: Quality and Recalls
summary: The partial document discusses a product recall issued in 2025 due to a weld seam defect in Harrier ST front forks. The company recalled 4,200 forks from batch H-2417 and dealers replaced them free of charge within six weeks. The supplier of the fork crowns was also changed, and incoming inspections now include X-ray testing of every fork crown batch.

title: Financial Summary
summary:
The main points covered in the partial document are:
- Revenue for 2025 increased by 9 percent to 12.4 million EUR compared to 2024.
- Export sales represented 31 percent of revenue, with Germany, the Netherlands, and Ireland being the top export markets.
- Gross margin improved to 27 percent, up one point from the previous year, attributed to lower aluminium spot prices.
- Operating expenses increased by 4 percent.
- The company achieved a small operating profit of 0.4 million EUR for the year.

title: Research and Outlook
summary: The partial document covers a research project on flax fibre composites initiated by the carbon laboratory in cooperation with Trent University, details of a daily commute programme using test frames, and plans for a prototype electric cargo bike named Mule 1 for 2026, with series production targeted for 2027.
